steps.text: About four thousand years ago, a king in the Indus Valley was carved wearing a cloak of three-leaf patterns. Was that cloth printed with a carved block? Nobody knows.
This is The Repeating Hand: an open-data history of block printing, the oldest way to copy a pattern. Every claim carries its source.
Meet the Priest-King in three-D, rebuilt from museum photographs. Turn him around, then switch the stone to printed cloth. That is an illustration of the idea, not evidence.
Every claim is sorted by how well it holds up: evidenced, reported, not found, or imagined. Nothing is passed off as settled.
Then follow the craft across the map: the first cotton at Mehrgarh, carved blocks in Egypt, Indian cottons found in Cairo, and the calico that changed Europe.
And it is free and open source. The code, the data and the three-D model are all in a public GitHub repo. Fork it, reuse it, and tell a different history.
